source.title: Outturn return: local authority expenditure on schools, other education and community for financial year 2015 to 2016 to financial year 2025 to 2026 (section 251 outturn), lines 1.8.1 / 1.9.3 'Dedicated Schools Grant carried forward' and 1.7.1 / 1.9.2 'brought forward'

cross_check.title: LA and school expenditure, financial year 2024-25 (official statistics, Explore Education Statistics) - 'LA expenditure on schools, other education and community - unrounded data'
cross_check.result: 1366 LA-year carry-forward values for 2015-16 to 2024-25 match the gov.uk file to the pound; 0 differ. The gov.uk file additionally has 2016-17, 2025-26 and Cumberland / Westmorland and Furness for 2023-24 (suppressed 'x' in EES).

notes: Values are pounds (cash, not inflation-adjusted), one per LA per financial year: the LA's net cumulative DSG position carried forward at 31 March, as the LA reported it in that year's section 251 outturn return.

Sign normalised to surplus positive, deficit negative. DfE's form records line 1.9.3 with the opposite sign from 2018-19 ('please show a deficit as a positive'); for 2015-16 to 2017-18 (lines 1.8.1 / 1.9.3, no stated convention) LAs mostly entered a surplus as positive: 80-86% of LAs' carry-forward matches the next year's brought-forward line (deficit negative) to within 5%, and nearly all the rest agree in sign.

Where the normalised carry-forward and the next year's brought-forward line disagree in sign (both over £100,000), the sign was taken from the brought-forward line (an LA sign-entry error); 22 such LA-years are listed in sign_corrections. Magnitudes are never changed.

A reported carry-forward of exactly 0 followed by a material (over £100,000) brought-forward balance the next year is treated as a missing entry and left out (9 LA-years, listed in omitted_values, all 2015-16 to 2018-19). Other early-year zeros are kept as reported.
Data quality is weaker before 2018-19, when the form first stated the sign convention; use 2015-16 to 2017-18 with care.

2025-26 is the newest year: data as submitted by LAs in the 2025-26 outturn collection (deadline 31 July 2026), published by DfE on gov.uk on 13 October 2026, before the 2025-26 official statistics release and before LA accounts are audited; treat as provisional. Earlier years are identical to the official statistics.

Whole DSG, not high needs only: the figure nets all four blocks (schools, central school services, early years, high needs). DfE notes there is no separate 'high needs deficit' in accounting terms, but almost all deficits come from high needs overspending (England 2025-26: high needs block in-year overspend £3.19bn against a whole-DSG in-year deficit of £2.88bn).

Statutory override: since 2020-21 DSG deficits are held in a separate unusable reserve rather than met from council general funds. The override runs to the end of 2027-28. Under the February 2026 approach, the High Needs Stability Grant pays 90% of each LA's eligible DSG deficit at 31 March 2026 from autumn 2026, so 2026-27 balances will fall sharply.

Safety Valve payments from DfE (recorded as in-year DSG adjustments) and any council top-ups (line 1.9.5) are already netted off, so Safety Valve LAs' deficits are shown after the bail-out money received to date.

Academies: the LA's DSG is after academy recoupment, and DfE pays high-needs place funding direct to academies, so neither appears. High-needs top-up funding that LAs pay to academies and colleges for pupils with EHC plans is LA DSG spending and is included. Academy trusts' own reserves or deficits are not included. Neither are maintained schools' own balances, which are reported separately.

Local government reorganisation: values sit under the code that reported them. Predecessor councils (Dorset 835, Poole 836, Bournemouth 837, Northamptonshire 928, Cumbria 909) are in former_las and not mapped to successors, because balances cannot be split. Successor series start in 2019-20 (838, 839), 2021-22 (940, 941) and 2023-24 (942, 943).
england is DfE's England total of the same line (sum of all LA returns, net of surpluses), sign-normalised. england_deficits_only is the sum over LAs in deficit, after sign corrections.

measure: Cumulative (net) Dedicated Schools Grant balance carried forward at 31 March of each financial year, in pounds: the LA's whole-DSG surplus or deficit from all years to date (all four DSG blocks combined, not high needs only), from section 251 outturn line 1.9.3 (1.8.1 before 2017-18). Negative = deficit, positive = surplus. Cash terms.

safety_valve.title: Dedicated schools grant: very high deficit intervention ('safety valve' agreements)
safety_valve.notes: 38 agreements: 5 in 2020-21, 9 in 2021-22, 20 in 2022-23, 4 in 2023-24. The programme closed on 1 April 2026 and was replaced by the High Needs Stability Grant (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/explanatory-note-on-the-governments-approach-to-dedicated-schools-grant-deficits).

delivering_better_value.title: Guidance on our intervention work with local authorities (Delivering Better Value in SEND, participating authorities), October 2022
delivering_better_value.notes: 55 authorities as listed by DfE in October 2022 (20 + 20 + 15 across three tranches). Cumbria (since split) is mapped to both Cumberland (942) and Westmorland and Furness (943); DfE's November 2023 DBV grant letter (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/delivering-better-value-in-send-implementation-plans-grant-determination-letter) pays both. Bracknell Forest, Bristol and Wiltshire later moved to Safety Valve (2023-24 agreements) and appear in both lists.
